requirements.summary: Baseline showed /tmp not separately mounted (cmd-1f4c4e0da02b4fc0). Executor added a tmpfs fstab entry with defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev and mounted it live; findmnt confirmed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec on /tmp both before (cmd-158738346f184826) and after a genuine reboot (cmd-b39aed9e08d84fb9). Functional exec tests denied execution with exit 126 before (cmd-fa588ea7c0cb4c2f) and after reboot (cmd-e05b304cdad84f3f).

Baseline /dev/shm had nosuid,nodev but not noexec (cmd-1f4c4e0da02b4fc0). Executor added a tmpfs fstab entry with defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev and remounted live; findmnt confirmed noexec,nosuid,nodev before (cmd-158738346f184826) and after reboot (cmd-b39aed9e08d84fb9). Functional exec denial confirmed on /dev/shm post-reboot (cmd-e05b304cdad84f3f); pre-reboot functional test only covered /tmp directly, but the mount-option confirmation covered both.

Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id and healthy state (cmd-808b31f44f164242). Reboot acknowledged and executed (cmd-f4e8444598c94c6f), connection reset observed (cmd-f332dcda12314aeb, cmd-e79750217b5d45ec), then a new boot_id was observed (cmd-7a6493a9f21d447a), independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity vs global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity). Post-reboot findmnt and functional tests confirmed the same options and enforcement persisted (cmd-b39aed9e08d84fb9, cmd-e05b304cdad84f3f), and system health was confirmed healthy both before and after (cmd-808b31f44f164242, cmd-e05b304cdad84f3f, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services empty).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes — /tmp with noexec/nosuid/nodev, /dev/shm with noexec/nosuid/nodev, and persistence across a genuine reboot — are directly and coherently demonstrated via fstab changes, live findmnt confirmation, functional exec-denial tests, and a full pre-restart/ack/post-restart boot-identity transition cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The task is fully satisfied with only a trivial hygiene ding for one leftover test script.
limitations: Pre-reboot functional exec test was only performed on /tmp; /dev/shm's noexec was confirmed pre-reboot only via findmnt option flags, not a live execution attempt (the execution attempt on /dev/shm was only done post-reboot).
A leftover test file (/tmp/t2.sh) was not cleaned up after verification, though it poses no functional or security risk on a noexec tmpfs.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor took a reasonable, bounded set of state-changing actions: backing up /etc/fstab before editing it (cmd-fc2626fa4cb940bd, backup retained but low-risk and a sensible precaution before modifying a critical system file), appending fstab entries (cmd-fc2626fa4cb940bd), reloading systemd and remounting/mounting /tmp and /dev/shm (cmd-e211043872804350), and creating small test scripts to functionally verify noexec enforcement (cmd-fa588ea7c0cb4c2f, cmd-e05b304cdad84f3f). All of these are directly tied to satisfying or verifying the material task outcome. One minor residue: the post-reboot test script /tmp/t2.sh was not removed and is visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot (added_lines includes /tmp/t2.sh); this is a small, low-risk leftover on a noexec tmpfs (not executable, no security impact) but was not cleaned up. No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes (listening-socket diffs are just PID churn from the reboot, not new services), and package health remained consistent (manager=dnf, no errors) before and after.
